kinds.d: Cured pork belly, back or loin sold in rashers or a piece to be cooked, smoked or unsmoked.

x.d: English bacon and ham cure developed by the Harris family at Calne in the 18th century; brine-cured since the First World War, smoked or green.
x.dt: back, streaky or middle · smoked or green

x.d: Scotland's distinctive cure: skinned, boned pork brined, then rolled as middle with streaky around the back.
Side bacon from the belly with layers of fat and lean; what "bacon" means in the US.
x.dt: thin or thick cut · smoke wood · cured or uncured

x.d: Unsmoked Toronto back bacon of wet-cured boneless loin rolled in cornmeal, credited to William Davies.
US name for back bacon from the loin, usually precooked and thick-sliced.

kinds.d: Pork hind leg wet- or dry-cured and sold raw as a joint or steaks to be cooked; once cooked it is ham.
Pork leg cured then cooked, sold whole or sliced, bone-in or boneless, glazed or plain.

x.d: Yorkshire-style dry-cured ham eaten boiled or baked; a generic curing style with no protected status.
Boneless brine-cured ham, stewed then lightly beech-smoked; EU TSG since 2018.
French steam-cooked ham with a mild flavour and delicate texture.

v.d: Label Rouge pork, restricted cure list

x.d: Italian wet-cured ham, brined, cooked in a mould and surface-pasteurised.
Ham cured by the Wiltshire brine method; a 2025 TSG bid for Wiltshire Cured Ham failed.
Black-skinned ham dry-salted then cured in molasses, coriander and juniper, aged six months and smoked; recipe dated 1781.

kinds.d: Beef brine-cured and cooked, usually brisket, also silverside (salt beef) or another cut, sold as a piece or sliced.

x.d: Brined brisket sold ready to eat in Jewish delicatessens; the meat of the Reuben sandwich.
Commonwealth name for salt-cured corned beef.
Salt beef sold in buckets of brine, used in Jiggs dinner.

kinds.d: Beef cured, seasoned, smoked and cooked, sold as a piece or sliced.

x.d: Jewish-American beef navel brined, spiced with pepper and coriander, smoked and steamed; served on rye.
Spiced brisket with more cracked pepper than pastrami, hot-smoked then steamed.
Romanian forerunner of pastrami, often of mutton, lamb or goat.

kinds.d: Ox or pork tongue brined, cooked and pressed, sold whole or sliced.

brands.d: Ann Arbor, Michigan delicatessen and mail-order food business.

notes: All six planned kinds kept with old sources. Zingerman's models became versions of the deli archetypes plus a brand entry.
